generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The `isClientCompatible` method's comment says the client's major version must be "at most one unit behind server's," but the condition `server.major - client.major <= 1` also passes when `client.major > server.major` (e.g., server=7, client=9 gives `7-9=-2 <= 1`). This is safe only because `server.onOrAfter(client)` is checked first and would reject that case. However, the conjunction order makes the safety implicit. Consider adding a brief comment noting that `server.onOrAfter(client)` is what prevents the client from being ahead, so the major-delta check only needs to bound the "behind" direction.

Two issues in `getNextVersion`:
1. The error message says `"couldn't find any released versions before"` but this is the *next* version lookup — it should say `"after"`.
2. There is no guard against a negative `index` from `Collections.binarySearch` when the version is not found in the list. If `index` is negative (e.g., -1), the condition `index >= DECLARED_VERSIONS.size() - 1` is `false`, and the code proceeds to `DECLARED_VERSIONS.get(index + 1)` — returning `DECLARED_VERSIONS.get(0)` for index -1, or throwing an `IndexOutOfBoundsException` for more negative values. A check like `if (index < 0)` should be added (or the combined condition should be `if (index < 0 || index >= DECLARED_VERSIONS.size() - 1)`).

The test builds a list by filtering `SqlVersions.getAllVersions()` and then appends `VersionTests.current()`. If `VersionTests.current()` happens to equal one of the versions already in the filtered list (e.g., if the build version is exactly 8.16.0), the list will contain a duplicate, causing the same version to be tested twice. This is harmless but slightly wasteful. More importantly, if `VersionTests.current()` is *before* `INTRODUCING_VERSION_COMPATIBILITY` (unlikely but possible with a very old build), it would be added to a list of "compatible" versions and the test would incorrectly expect no exception.

These three sites convert `SqlVersion` back to `Version`/`TransportVersion` via `.id` (e.g., `Version.fromId(INTRODUCING_UNSIGNED_LONG.id)`, `TransportVersion.fromId(INTRODUCING_UNSIGNED_LONG.id)`). This round-trip through the integer ID is fragile: it assumes the ID encoding in `SqlVersion` is identical to `Version`/`TransportVersion`. If the two systems ever diverge in their ID scheme, these conversions would silently produce wrong versions. A brief comment at each site (or a shared helper) noting this assumption would help future maintainers.

`SqlVersion.fromString` returns `null` for null/empty input (per the dependency shown). All three sites call it with `Build.current().version()` without a null check:
```java
public static final SqlVersion CURRENT = SqlVersion.fromString(Build.current().version());
```
If `Build.current().version()` ever returns null or an empty string, `CURRENT` will be `null`, and every downstream use (`.major`, `.minor`, `.onOrAfter(...)`) will throw a `NullPointerException` with no clear cause. Consider adding a null-guard or using `Objects.requireNonNull` with a descriptive message.

review_comment: Ah, `SqlVersion` doesn't implement `VersionId`. If it implements `VersionId<T>` then this method will come for free
Right, there's no `.before()` method and `SqlVersion` can't implement `VersionId<T>`, since it's in a package very light in dependencies.

This is the `minCompatibleShardNode` - which is still a `Version`. If the version is locked at 8.16, this means this parameter can be completely removed on v9 and replaced with another mechanism if/when SQL needs to be updated?

> this means this parameter can be completely removed on v9

I would think so, assuming that we have an upgrade procedure to 9.x similar to [the existing 7.x to 8.x one](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elastic-stack/current/upgrading-elastic-stack.html#prepare-to-upgrade): upgrade to the latest 8.x one and then the target 9.x. This would mean that the SearchRequest wouldn't need to be given a min (shard) version, since all the nodes in the cluster would respect that condition already.

> and replaced with another mechanism if/when SQL needs to be updated?

I think the above would stand independent on SQL being updated or not.
OK - After this is merged, I'll look at removing that then
